name: Borussia Dortmund 2010–13
scopeNote: Borussia Dortmund under Klopp across 2010/11 to 2012/13: from the DFB-Pokal first round win at Wacker Burghausen (14 Aug 2010, 3-0) to the Champions League final defeat to Bayern Munich at Wembley (25 May 2013, 1-2). Bundesliga titles 2010/11 (clinched 30 Apr 2011) and 2011/12 (81 points, plus the DFB-Pokal for the double), 2nd in 2012/13. Style: Gegenpressing from a 4-2-3-1 with fast vertical transitions (Spielverlagerung 2011: "Gegenpressing direkt nach Ballverlust"; Klopp's own label "heavy metal", 2013). Exact match totals not read from a source; the period is well above the ~15-match minimum. One manager throughout. Note: Wikipedia lists a DFL-Supercup in July/Aug 2011 inside 2011/12; it falls inside the period.
openQuestions: Marking (mar): Breaking The Lines says the press early on 'looked like a man-oriented press' and was then supplemented by Raum-Deckung, without dating the change; Klopp (2026) calls ball-oriented defending / Raumdeckung his base. No source dates the shift to 2010-13 seasons. Confirm how to read it (likely ball-oriented zonal base with man-oriented pressing jumps).
Set pieces: no source read covers Dortmund set pieces in this period.

Possession: only a Spielverlagerung preparation note (Ballbesitz focus in 2010/11 pre-season); no possession figures. The 2012/13 final is long balls to Lewandowski, so Gegenpressing / counter vs possession reading rests on few facts.

The 2010/11 formation after Kagawa's injury and the 2011/12 shape (Gündogan, Kagawa, Götze, Lewandowski) lack a season-specific tactical analysis; shapes rest on a 2011 portrait and a 2022 retrospective (mostly 2012/13).

Most tactical sources are retrospective or era-wide (Sky 2020, TFA 2020, BTL 2022); only Spielverlagerung 2011 and 2013 and schwatzgelb 2011 are contemporary. No in-period Klopp quote on his tactics found; stated view comes from Nov 2013 (just after the period) and 2026.

Pressing height: Sky says medium block rarely full-pitch; Spielverlagerung's final describes 'direct attacking pressing' in a 4-4-2 with a high line. Confirm whether to treat 2013 as a distinct, higher-pressing variant.

sources.title: Jürgen Klopp, der Menschenfänger (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: "die offensive Dreierreihe im 4-2-3-1-System" in 2010/11; the attacking three pushed far into the middle. After Kagawa's injury Klopp was "gezwungen sein System zur Rückrunde umzustellen".

sources.title: Jürgen Klopp, der Menschenfänger (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: "ruhiger Spielaufbau über die Innenverteidiger"; Sahin to help against deep-lying opponents.

sources.title: Jürgen Klopp, der Menschenfänger (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Preparation for 2010/11 put the focus on Ballbesitzspiel ("auf das Ballbesitzspiel zu legen"). Paraphrase from page; no possession figures.

sources.title: Jürgen Klopp, der Menschenfänger (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: "Gegenpressing direkt nach Ballverlust" and "Schnelles vertikales Spiel nach Ballgewinn in Mittelfeld oder Angriff".

sources.title: Jürgen Klopp, der Menschenfänger (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Paraphrase: Piszczek played more centrally, "nicht mehr so sehr an der Außenlinie"; Błaszczykowski was more of a classic winger.

sources.title: Jürgen Klopp, der Menschenfänger (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Champion team "in der nur Torhüter Weidenfeller älter als 26 Jahre war"; Hummels-Subotić pair called "Kinderriegel"; Klopp interlocks youth and professionals.

sources.title: Jürgen Klopp, der Menschenfänger (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Klopp dealt with different types (Zidan, Kehl) "den einzelnen Typen gerecht zu werden"; Watzke: "So einen Menschenfänger habe ich noch nicht kennen gelernt."

sources.title: Jürgen Klopp, der Menschenfänger (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Page mentions Raumdeckung only as introduced in Germany by Wolfgang Frank at Mainz ("die Raumdeckung"); it does not say how Dortmund defended in 2010/11. Context only.

sources.title: Tactical Analysis: Jürgen Klopp's Borussia Dortmund (Breaking The Lines)
sources.evidence: "The basic setup on paper was the 4-2-3-1", shifting to a 2-2-6 in possession; v Real Madrid out of possession "maintained a 4-1-4-1/4-4-2 shape" (examples mainly 2012/13).

sources.title: Tactical Analysis: Jürgen Klopp's Borussia Dortmund (Breaking The Lines)
sources.evidence: Hummels "was responsible for organizing the build-up in phase 1"; intent "a vertical pass breaking the lines"; when Gündogan was marked Klopp dropped him into a back three with Hummels and Subotić.

sources.title: Tactical Analysis: Jürgen Klopp's Borussia Dortmund (Breaking The Lines)
sources.evidence: Early on the press "looked like a man-oriented press" with players close together; it was "proving to be unsustainable over a season with the same intensity", so Klopp added Raum-Deckung. Aim: close down "in Phase 1 of the transition within 8 seconds". V Madrid: "Press high and isolate Alonso." Article does not date the man-oriented phase to a season, so kept unverified for the period.

sources.title: Tactical Analysis: Jürgen Klopp's Borussia Dortmund (Breaking The Lines)
sources.evidence: Raum-Deckung aimed at "closing down passing lanes to prevent progression"; v Madrid "narrow and compact", shifting into a "4-5-1 block" to guard the half-spaces.

sources.title: Tactical Analysis: Jürgen Klopp's Borussia Dortmund (Breaking The Lines)
sources.evidence: "entering the final third as soon as possible"; "systematic counter-attacking"; "Dortmund was first to arrive at every 2nd ball" v Real Madrid (2013 semi-final).

sources.title: Tactical Analysis: Jürgen Klopp's Borussia Dortmund (Breaking The Lines)
sources.evidence: Wide players tucked in while "the fullbacks pushing high"; wingers valued for "holding width, crossing and arriving late at the far post".

sources.title: Tactical Analysis: Jürgen Klopp's Borussia Dortmund (Breaking The Lines)
sources.evidence: Reus, Gündoğan, Lewandowski and Götze "were players who were quick on and off the ball"; Götze "was really good in tight spaces".

sources.title: Tactical Analysis: Jürgen Klopp's Borussia Dortmund (Breaking The Lines)
sources.evidence: Klopp "created the core of this team around hard-working young players" who "lacked in quality" but made up with "superb intensity and organization".

sources.title: Tactical Analysis: Jürgen Klopp's Borussia Dortmund (Breaking The Lines)
sources.evidence: Plan changes by opponent: against Real Madrid, "Press high and isolate Alonso" and a 4-5-1 block; when Gündoğan was marked Klopp changed the build-up to a back three.

sources.title: Borussia Dortmund - Bayern Munich 1:2, Champions League final (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: V Bayern: "Lewandowski and Reus pushed out side by side in a 4-4-2, just in front of the opposing central defenders"; "Against the ball, the BVB was positioned in direct attacking pressing"; they controlled "the crucial key points and pass routes" rather than hunting the centre-backs. The man-orientation named on the page is Bayern's. One match.

sources.title: Borussia Dortmund - Bayern Munich 1:2, Champions League final (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: "Dortmund's high position carried the risk that small errors could become extremely dangerous"; after about 20 minutes they "positioned themselves somewhat deeper". One match.

sources.title: Borussia Dortmund - Bayern Munich 1:2, Champions League final (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: "Besides the counter-attacks, the BVB acted mostly with long balls to Lewandowski." One match.

sources.title: Borussia Dortmund - Bayern Munich 1:2, Champions League final (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: After Bayern's 60th-minute goal "Borussia took more of a risk in build-up play" and the full-backs "pushed forward earlier"; Klopp "opted for the established alternative" with Reus central. One match.

sources.title: Why Jurgen Klopp's gegenpressing with Dortmund was revolutionary (Sky Sports)
sources.evidence: "Dortmund rarely used a full-pitch press, because doing so encouraged the opposition to kick the ball long." Typically a medium block, pressing once the ball reached full-backs or midfielders; they "piled players into the immediate vicinity of the player in possession". Era-level, undated.

sources.title: Why Jurgen Klopp's gegenpressing with Dortmund was revolutionary (Sky Sports)
sources.evidence: "They were perfectly solid without possession, and defending deep actually suited their counter-attacking."

sources.title: Why Jurgen Klopp's gegenpressing with Dortmund was revolutionary (Sky Sports)
sources.evidence: Wide midfielders "usually Kevin Grosskreutz and Jakub Blaszczykowski, tucked inside".

sources.title: Klopp: his tactical evolution from Dortmund to Liverpool (Total Football Analysis)
sources.evidence: Dortmund "attacked with a rather narrow shape"; in a mid-block "a compact 4-4-1-1 against Bayern" with the two forwards using cover shadows. Match and season not dated on the page.

sources.title: Klopp: his tactical evolution from Dortmund to Liverpool (Total Football Analysis)
sources.evidence: Triggers: "A bad pass, miscontrol of the ball or a closed body shape of a receiving player"; if the opponent passed backwards Dortmund "would not necessarily continue their press". Does not address zonal vs man.

sources.title: Klopp: his tactical evolution from Dortmund to Liverpool (Total Football Analysis)
sources.evidence: "Dortmund would often build up their play through one side of the pitch"; overload on the right leaves space on the left, but the left-back sat too deep so they "fail to switch sides".

sources.title: Klopp: his tactical evolution from Dortmund to Liverpool (Total Football Analysis)
sources.evidence: Klopp "especially attempted to bring the defensive transitioning of his team to perfection" with a quick press after losing the ball.

sources.title: Jurgen Klopp: how Borussia Dortmund won the 2010/11 German top flight (bundesliga.com)
sources.evidence: Klopp's side were "further down the line with their aggressive pressing and rapid counter-attacks" (matchday 10 v Mainz).

sources.title: Jurgen Klopp: how Borussia Dortmund won the 2010/11 German top flight (bundesliga.com)
sources.evidence: Matchday 24 side in Munich was "the youngest team in their Bundesliga history - with an average age of 22.3 years"; "Germany's youngest ever champions". Piszczek from Hertha Berlin, Kagawa from Cerezo Osaka, Lewandowski from Lech Poznan.

sources.title: Jurgen Klopp: how Borussia Dortmund won the 2010/11 German top flight (bundesliga.com)
sources.evidence: Watzke (2019): "In this year of the first title, he was a locomotive who gave the power to the rest." Hummels: Klopp introduced a system that worked and a desire to "give it everything and go the extra yard".

sources.title: Major Klopp - championship maker (schwatzgelb.de)
sources.evidence: "The extreme flexibility of Die Borussen's tactics allowed them to adapt to and defeat their opponents' strategies." Also "intense pressing whenever an opponent had possession", "lightning-fast counterattacks in numbers".

sources.title: Major Klopp - championship maker (schwatzgelb.de)
sources.evidence: "With an average age of just 23"; "Klopp managed to motivate and mould a young, raw, and inexperienced squad into a team of title-winners."

sources.title: How Jurgen Klopp built an empire out of ruin at Borussia Dortmund (These Football Times)
sources.evidence: Błaszczykowski and Lewandowski bought "for a pittance from Poland"; Subotić, Hummels, Bender, Großkreutz and Piszczek "for similarly small sums from an assortment of German rivals"; Götze "promoted from within"; Klopp drew "astutely from his club's youth academy". Retrospective.

sources.title: How Jurgen Klopp built an empire out of ruin at Borussia Dortmund (These Football Times)
sources.evidence: "lightning-quick transitions from defence to attack" and "gegenpressing, or counter-pressing"; an "aggressive, exuberant, albeit exhausting, fast-paced system". Retrospective.

sources.title: Wie gut war eigentlich Borussia Dortmund von 2010 bis 2013? (90min.de)
sources.evidence: Paraphrase from the page: Klopp's teams played intense Gegenpressing from a 4-2-3-1 with fast transitions; the core stayed together for years; 2010/11 Europa League and 2011/12 Champions League exits came in the group stage. Page reader gave a summary, not verbatim quotes.

sources.title: Iconic teams: Dortmund double winners 2011/12 (bundesliga.com)
sources.evidence: Gündoğan arrived summer 2011 "something of an unknown"; Kagawa's "technique and creative vision consistently had opponents in knots"; Kehl was "doing the dirty work so that those around him could express themselves"; Hummels and Subotić the "foundation of the side". No tactics on the page.

statedView.quote: It's like an orchestra, but they play a silent song. I like heavy metal, I always want it to be loud.
Arsenal have a philosophy from Arsene Wenger, I love that, but I can't coach that way, I am different.
Gegenpressing lets you win back the ball nearer to the goal. It's only one pass away from a really good opportunity.
Für andere sah es chaotisch aus, für uns war es organisiert.
das ballorientierte Verteidigen, also die Raumdeckung, eingeführt wurde.

influences.note: Gegenpressing, coined and practised by Klopp's Dortmund; Raumdeckung learnt from Wolfgang Frank at Mainz.

confidence.reason: Contemporary tier B evidence (Spielverlagerung 2011 and the 2013 final) agrees with era-level tier B-C pieces on a 4-2-3-1 Gegenpressing team with fast vertical transitions and a very young squad, but most pieces are retrospective or era-wide, season-specific detail for 2011/12 is thin, set pieces are uncovered, marking is not dated, and the stated view is from outside the period.
